    "title": "In-place downsizing can destroy animated GIF originals and ignores conversion failures",
    "body": "`OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, '80%', allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` uses the original upload as both input and output. If `allow_animated_thumbnails` is false, `OptimizedImage.optimize` picks the non-animated `downsize_instructions`, whose ImageMagick command reads only `#{from}[0]` (the first frame) and writes to `#{to}`. Because `from == to`, a large animated GIF upload is replaced by a static resized first frame and the animation is permanently lost. Also `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false` on conversion failure rather than raising, but the return value is ignored; after up to five attempts the code proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with the possibly unchanged, oversized, or partially overwritten file. Downscale to a separate temp file, check the result, and never mutate the original upload path directly."
  },

    "category": "api",
    "title": "Second `downsize` definition overrides the existing 4-argument method",
    "body": "Ruby does not overload class methods by arity. Defining `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 completely replaces the previous `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145. Existing code that calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height, opts)` will either raise `ArgumentError` (when five arguments are passed) or bind the height integer to `opts`, causing a later `TypeError` in `optimize` when `opts[:allow_animation]` is accessed. Keep one method and explicitly support both call forms or update all callers."
  },
  {
    "file": "app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js",
    "line": 182,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Client upload size validation is hardcoded to 10MB instead of using site settings",
    "body": "`validateUploadedFile` now sets `maxSizeKB` to `10 * 1024` for every upload type instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, and the 413 handler at line 246 does the same for `max_image_size_kb`. This disables configured `max_image_size_kb` / `max_attachment_size_kb` limits in the client: sites with a larger limit reject valid files before upload, and sites with a smaller limit do not warn before the upload is rejected server-side. It is especially wrong for attachments because server-side auto-downsizing only applies to images."
  },
  {
    "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
    "line": 55,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "api",
    "title": "API URL download limit is hardcoded to 10MB",
    "body": "`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the configured `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` with a constant. API URL uploads are now capped at 10MB even when the site allows larger files (or has no such small cap), and the setting is ignored for this path. If the intent is to download a larger original before downscaling it, the download cap should be derived from the site setting or a separate explicit setting, not fixed to 10MB."
  }

findings.title: In-place downsizing can destroy animated GIF originals and ignores conversion failures
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, '80%', allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` uses the original upload as both input and output. If `allow_animated_thumbnails` is false, `OptimizedImage.optimize` picks the non-animated `downsize_instructions`, whose ImageMagick command reads only `#{from}[0]` (the first frame) and writes to `#{to}`. Because `from == to`, a large animated GIF upload is replaced by a static resized first frame and the animation is permanently lost. Also `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns `false` on conversion failure rather than raising, but the return value is ignored; after up to five attempts the code proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with the possibly unchanged, oversized, or partially overwritten file. Downscale to a separate temp file, check the result, and never mutate the original upload path directly.

findings.title: Second `downsize` definition overrides the existing 4-argument method
findings.body: Ruby does not overload class methods by arity. Defining `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 completely replaces the previous `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at line 145. Existing code that calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height, opts)` will either raise `ArgumentError` (when five arguments are passed) or bind the height integer to `opts`, causing a later `TypeError` in `optimize` when `opts[:allow_animation]` is accessed. Keep one method and explicitly support both call forms or update all callers.

findings.title: Client upload size validation is hardcoded to 10MB instead of using site settings
findings.body: `validateUploadedFile` now sets `maxSizeKB` to `10 * 1024` for every upload type instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, and the 413 handler at line 246 does the same for `max_image_size_kb`. This disables configured `max_image_size_kb` / `max_attachment_size_kb` limits in the client: sites with a larger limit reject valid files before upload, and sites with a smaller limit do not warn before the upload is rejected server-side. It is especially wrong for attachments because server-side auto-downsizing only applies to images.

findings.title: API URL download limit is hardcoded to 10MB
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the configured `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` with a constant. API URL uploads are now capped at 10MB even when the site allows larger files (or has no such small cap), and the setting is ignored for this path. If the intent is to download a larger original before downscaling it, the download cap should be derived from the site setting or a separate explicit setting, not fixed to 10MB.
